items.title: Benny Golson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Bobby Timmons, I got him to finish that tune he thought was no good, Moanin’.

ctx.x: So you resume off and on in various configurations the Jazztet, but you also get back with Art Blakey again, who you helped to get on the track. You did several reunions.

He stayed on the track, too. He really did. The money stayed up. He presented the group in a good way. He learned how – when to take the intermission, to come back. It was so messed up before. When he was playing Small’s Paradise before I joined him, he would play – an intermission was 20 minutes, and he would be gone an hour, an hour and a half. They said they never wanted him back in there again. So when I took the group over, I said, “We have to set goals for ourselves. One of the goals – one of the first…

According to this chronology, you were with Art Blakey again in ’83 and then again in ’89. He passed in ’90. What was it like coming back, working with Art Blakey? He still had that same fire, that same magic?
